instantiated_cells.justification: The periodic expense statement filing requirement applies to registered principals, not to lobbyists filing their own spending reports.
The only periodic spending report described is the principal’s semiannual expense statement, not a lobbyist’s report, so there is no lobbyist semiannual spending-report cadence.
Statute requires principals to file semiannual expense statements and requires lobbyists only to provide information to principals, not to file annual lobbyist spending reports.
No provision requires lobbyists to file monthly spending reports; periodic reports are filed by principals on July 31 and January 31.
The statute sets semiannual principal filing dates and does not establish any quarterly lobbyist spending report.
There is no triannual lobbyist spending report in the statute; reporting is a principal obligation on two dates per year.
The statute does not create any other lobbyist periodic spending-report cadence; lobbyists provide information to principals who file.
Section 13.68 imposes the periodic expense-statement filing duty on principals, not lobbyists, so there is no lobbyist spending-report filing cadence.
Total lobbying expenditures are reported by the principal in its expense statement, not in a lobbyist-filed spending report.
Compensation to lobbyists is included in the aggregate total that the principal reports, but lobbyists are not required to file their own report disclosing total compensation.

Any breakdown of compensation is in the principal’s filing (e.g., amounts paid to each lobbyist over $200), and lobbyists themselves only supply information to the principal rather than file a payer-broken-down report.
The statute’s required expense categorization applies to principal filings, and it does not require lobbyists to file a categorized spending report.

Lobbyists must provide supporting information to principals for the principal’s expense statement, but the statute does not require lobbyists to file itemized expenses with the commission as a periodic spending report.
Only principals file expense statements; lobbyists do not file a periodic report in any itemized format.
Identifiers for legislative proposals and proposed administrative rules are reported by principals under §13.67, not by lobbyists in a spending report.

The statute requires principals to report each 'legislative proposal' and 'proposed administrative rule number' connected to lobbying communications, but does not impose an analogous lobbyist spending-report requirement.
Topics/general issues must be reported by the principal to the commission, not by lobbyists via periodic spending reports.
General subject-matter reporting (topics described with reasonable specificity) is a principal obligation and not part of a lobbyist periodic spending report.
Section 13.67 requires reporting of proposals/topics but does not require any filer (and specifically not lobbyists) to report positions on bills in a spending report.
The daily itemization of time spent meeting with officials is required in the principal’s expense statement record, not in a lobbyist-filed contacts report.
The only per-issue disclosure is a principal’s estimate of proportion of time by proposal/topic, not a lobbyist spending report of expenditures per issue.
Gifts, lodging, transportation, and meals are largely prohibited for lobbyists/principals to furnish, but there is no lobbyist periodic spending-report requirement to disclose such expenditures.
Indirect/overhead lobbying costs are included in the principal’s expense statement requirements, not in a lobbyist-filed spending report.
Lobbyists provide contact/residence information on the license application, but the statute does not require lobbyists to disclose address/phone in a periodic spending report.

Principal-lobbyist relationships are disclosed through written authorizations filed with the commission, but lobbyists are not required to file periodic spending reports listing all principals represented.
Principal name and business address are included in the principal’s registration statement, not in a lobbyist periodic spending report.
Descriptions of the principal’s business activity/nature and purposes are required in principal registration filings, not in lobbyist spending reports.
Because lobbyists are not required to file periodic spending reports at all, the statute does not require lobbyists to file a 'no activity' report.
The statute contains no lobbyist periodic spending-report requirement and thus does not define its scope to include spending benefiting household members of officials.
